# Code of Conduct

## Our Standard

Sentri is an open-source project for building practical student tooling. Contributors are expected to keep discussion respectful, specific, and focused on improving the project.

Examples of encouraged behavior:

- Use welcoming and inclusive language.
- Give constructive feedback with enough context to act on.
- Respect different experience levels and viewpoints.
- Keep disagreements technical and evidence-based.
- Accept maintainer decisions after concerns have been heard.

Examples of unacceptable behavior:

- Harassment, insults, threats, or personal attacks.
- Discriminatory language or conduct.
- Publishing private information without permission.
- Repeated off-topic disruption of issues, pull requests, or discussions.
- Any conduct that maintainers reasonably consider unsafe or abusive.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may remove comments, close issues, block users, or reject contributions that violate this code of conduct. Enforcement should be proportional to the behavior and focused on keeping the project usable for contributors.

## Reporting

Report conduct concerns through a private maintainer contact channel when available. If no private channel is available, open a short issue asking for a maintainer contact without including sensitive details.

## Scope

This code applies in project spaces including GitHub issues, pull requests, discussions, and any official project communication channels.
